question: In 1930 Keynes forecast that by 2030 living standards would be four to eight times higher and working weeks fifteen hours. How has it gone?
options: Incomes on track; hours far off
Hours on track; incomes far off
answer: Incomes on track; hours far off. Real income per head in Britain and the United States has risen roughly five- to eightfold since 1930, inside Keynes's range: growth of 2% a year compounds to about sevenfold in a century. Weekly hours fell only modestly. The riches arrived; the leisure mostly did not.
move: Before calling a century forecast wild, compound the growth rate yourself.
trap: Assuming an eightfold rise in a century must be fantasy.
source: Pecchi and Piga, Revisiting Keynes, MIT Press, 2008
reference: Pecchi & Piga (eds.), Revisiting Keynes: Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren, MIT Press, 2008
